 By STACY LIBERATORE, US SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EDITOR 
 Published: 12:57 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EST, 17 November 2026 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Apple became the latest major company to be plunged into chaos on Tuesday as a wave of technology outages and cyberattacks rattled the US. 
 The disruption comes on the heels of the National Security Agency (NSA)’s top-secret communications network going down and a cyberattack that spread malicious code to websites linked to 178 organizations , including CNN, Zoom and HSBC.
 Apple’s system status page flagged a problem with iCloud Account & Sign In, warning: ‘All users are affected. This service may be slow or unavailable.’
 Downdetector recorded sharp spikes in reports of problems with iCloud, Apple Pay, the App Store and Apple Support.
 Some iPhone users reported being prompted to re-enter their Apple Account passwords, only to receive the message: ‘Verification Failed – An unknown error occurred.’ Customers also report Apple retail store systems are down, disrupting order pickups and service appointments.
 Multiple major banks, including Chase and Bank of America, were also hit by technical issues on Monday, while Microsoft suffered a major blackout last week.
 Even though there is no confirmed connection between the system failures, the disruptions have ramped up concerns about whether America’s digital infrastructure is up to date. Pressure is now building on the Trump administration and Congress to investigate, and critics are calling for the White House to be fully transparent about the cause.
 The problems for Apple customers could extend far beyond logging into their accounts - with iPhone, iPad and Mac users potentially unable to access emails, photos and files.
 Apple is experiencing an outage affecting several iPhone services, leaving some users unable to access their accounts 
 Apple showed issues hit iCloud Account & Sign In around 11.45am ET. 
 Some user complaints began surfacing online, but the outage became more apparent just after 1pm, with issue reports coming from every state in the US.

 The complaints suggested problems spanning multiple Apple services, but the company has not publicly established whether they stemmed from the same outage. 
 The sign-in disruption can prevent users from accessing their Apple accounts on iPhones, iPads and Macs, potentially interfering with access to email, photos and files stored in iCloud.
 Affected users may encounter repeated password requests, verification errors or unexpected sign-outs. Problems could also arise when downloading apps, activating new devices or accessing services that require an Apple Account login.
 Cybersecurity expert James Knight told the Daily Mail: 'When Apple sign-in breaks, it isn’t just one app. Your Apple ID is the key to iCloud, Apple Pay, the App Store and even setting up a new phone, so one failure point locks people out of a lot at once. 
 'Right now, the public reporting points to a sign-in and account problem, and Apple hasn’t said what caused it, so nobody should call it an attack yet. What people should do is simple.' The Daily Mail has contacted Apple for comment.
 Apple's issues come just hours after the NSA Net network, which employees use for highly classified internal communications, went down Tuesday morning, six people familiar with the situation told CNN.
 One customer said they were at an Apple Store to get a new phone when staff told them the store’s systems, including internal platforms, were down (stock)
 Staff have been warned of a 'heightened security threat,' a source told the Daily Mail. Employees have also been told to stagger their arrivals at the NSA facility.
 Another source indicated that some areas that are operated by the NSA could be experiencing different levels of networking issues than others.
 The NSA has not confirmed what caused the outage, but officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack.
 A source familiar with the situation attributed the outage to a software update intended to 'patch' the NSA Net system, The Wall Street Journal reported. The insider added the network would be 'offline only temporarily.'
 The outage will not impact the NSA's ability to communicate any urgent intelligence to Trump while he is traveling, a current and former US official told CNN.
 The agency reportedly has multiple redundancies and backup networks that it can use for secure communications with the president, the sources added.
 iPhone users are receiving error messages when attempting to activate new devices 
 The NSA's network crash followed news that hackers targeted 178 of the world's biggest companies in a massive cyberattack on Monday. 
 Security researchers at Report URI identified malicious code in website tools used by 178 organizations, including Zoom, CNN, the BBC, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, Peacock, IKEA, Fox News, NPR, the ASPCA and Invisalign.
 The attack, detected Monday evening, targeted Optimizely, a service companies use to test different website layouts and features.
 Hackers used its customization tool to insert malicious code into webpages. It was delivered alongside genuine software through Optimizely’s trusted systems, making the threat harder to detect.
 The cybercriminals’ malicious software was designed to steal cryptocurrency payments, capture credit card details entered into certain online forms and hack iPhones and iPads with security weaknesses.
 Researchers reported cryptocurrency transfers to wallets controlled by the attackers, amounting to more than $7,000 so far. However, the number of people whose card details were stolen or devices successfully hacked remains unknown.
 The cyberattack follows a string of disruptions to essential services, including a global Microsoft outage and Friday’s nationwide grounding of flights.
 Customers at several major US banks also reported problems accessing online services on Monday, adding to a turbulent few days for the country’s critical systems.
